title: soalnya — because (casual)
pattern: A, soalnya B · A. Soalnya B.
explanation: soalnya is how people really say because in conversation. It comes after whatever it explains and starts the reason: Aku pulang duluan, soalnya capek. — I'm heading off first, I'm tired. It can also open a new sentence that adds the reason after a pause (Maaf, saya tidak bisa datang. Soalnya anak saya sakit.), or stand alone as the answer to Kenapa?: Soalnya hujan. habisnya (or just habis) gives a reason with a grumble in it, as if it's not your fault: Aku nggak beli, habisnya mahal banget.
natural: Everyday speech with friends, family and colleagues, and even politely, with saya and Bapak or Ibu, when you're explaining yourself. habisnya is for friends and family.
stiff: soalnya never comes before the point it explains: Karena hujan, … works, but a sentence can't open with Soalnya hujan, … and carry on; put it after: …, soalnya hujan. In writing, emails or anything formal, use karena.

examples.english: I'm heading off first, I'm tired.

gap.note: karena is right too, but among friends it sounds more careful than soalnya.
gap.why: soalnya starts the reason, after what it explains.

examples.english: Take an umbrella, it's going to rain.

gap.why: The rain is the reason to take an umbrella, so it follows soalnya.

examples.indonesian: Maaf, saya tidak bisa datang. Soalnya anak saya sakit.
examples.english: Sorry, I can't come. My child's ill, you see.

gap.why: Soalnya can open a new sentence that gives the reason for the one before.

examples.indonesian: Aku nggak beli, habisnya mahal banget.
examples.english: I didn't buy it, it was way too expensive.

gap.note: soalnya works too; habisnya adds a note of complaint, as if it's not your fault.
gap.why: habisnya gives a reason with a grumble in it.
